title: PREREG.md's registered predictions, re-stated as claims a record can refute. This file does NOT amend PREREG.md and is not one of its amendments: the sealed document remains the authority for what was predicted, and this restates those predictions in a form tools/record_claims.py can test. Added 2026-09-06 by experiments/2026-09-06-change-record-claims/.

claims.statement: The organiser seat never cites an evidence id the legend does not expose.
claims.note: The citation check is emitted from rules/conj.py, the conjecturer rule, so on a root whose only conjecturer shell is the organiser every hit is the organiser's. The three codes are the three ways a reference fails to name one exposed block: unknown to the dossier, admitted but not in the legend, or resolving to more than one block (src/deepreason/evidence/citations.py). A quote that mismatches is a different failure and is ORG-COND-01's.

claims.statement: Every conjecturer section plan names the organiser's own output contract as a rendered section.
claims.note: PREREG.md section 8, the operational prediction: 'ARM R's section plans name dr.output-contract.organiser on every conjecturer call'. Two halves, both needed: the run recorded at least one section plan, and no plan of the organiser layout omits the contract. Without the first half a run that rendered no brief at all would pass this claim vacuously; without the second, a plan carrying an empty sections list would. This is the record's form of 'every seat's section plan names its directive': the directive is what the output contract section carries, and the section plan is where the record says it was rendered.

claims.statement: A conjecturer section plan never names the ordinary conjecturer output contract.
claims.note: PREREG.md section 8, the second half of the same prediction: 'and never dr.output-contract.conjecturer'.
PREREG.md section 3: 'An operational_failure or a refused launch is a FAILED arm.'

claims.statement: The argumentative critic seat never terminally exhausts its smallest authorized contract.
claims.note: Read the standing before reading the survival. This root DOES carry a route-seat exhaustion, and it is the CONJECTURER's, not the critic's; the claim is about the critic and survives for that reason alone.

claims.statement: A candidate never registers an evidence citation that fails its check.
claims.note: PROXY, and the record cannot do better. The prediction it re-states is 'every countercondition registered came from a room proposal', and the record types no countercondition and no proposal-provenance: 'countercondition' occurs only inside artifact content prose. What the record DOES type is whether each evidence reference a candidate made resolves to an admitted block and whether its quote matches. A citation that fails is a candidate leaning on something the room did not supply as claimed. A citation that passes does not prove the countercondition came from a proposal; this claim can be refuted, it cannot be confirmed, and it is marked a proxy for the same reason h-EPI marks its own.

claims.statement: A run reaches a completed typed terminal.
claims.note: PREREG.md section 8, the operational prediction: 'both arms reach a clean typed terminal at cycle 4 or on budget'. An operational health check, not a success condition (CLAUDE.md, 2026-09-03).

claims.statement: The organiser seat never cites a block that is admitted but withheld from the legend.
claims.note: PREREG.md section 8 predicted the opposite in as many words: 'at least one EVIDENCE_REF_NOT_EXPOSED measure appears in the record', because the seat reads 94 blocks and can cite 32. Read the standing: if this claim survives with the condition never having held, the prediction did not come true and this check could not have failed.

claims.statement: The harness-alone arm never stops operational_failure.
claims.note: PREREG.md Amendment 3 deferred ARM H; it was never launched, so no root satisfies this scope and the claim is NOT_TESTED. That is the honest reading of a deferred arm, and it is why the scope is declared rather than left open: an open scope would have tested this against ARM R's root and reported a refutation of a claim about a run that does not exist.
